rv.q: This odd little show has charm aplenty, though for some it may also prove something of a well-intentioned dog’s dinner.
Giving human voices to pets was something of a double-edged sword in this case.

If grown-up actors playing children weren’t bad enough, in the Southwark Playhouse’s new show we now have grown-up actors playing dogs. This might be fine if Dog Mom were aimed at kids who might be delighted to see two adults sniffing each other’s butts, but apparently, with its swear words, this show is for an older audience.
Dog Mom has bags of heart, but it could dig deeper.
By taking itself a touch too seriously, “Dog Mom” weakens the messages that are better served with humour.
Well meaning canine comedy goes astray.

cn.t: This canine comedy about a woman and her dogs elicits mixed-to-negative reviews. Critics praise the talking dog characters as a joy, but find the human characters underdeveloped and the well-meaning premise doesn't fully deliver.
